doseResponse.code:
# Fit an Emax dose-response model to every patient:
#   response = E0 + Emax * dose / (ED50 + dose)
fit <- nls(response_pct ~ E0 + Emax * dose_mg / (ED50 + dose_mg),
           data = patients, start = list(E0 = 0, Emax = 40, ED50 = 50))
# Predict the curve over the tested range.
doses <- seq(0, 200, by = 25)
result <- data.frame(
  dose = paste(doses, "mg"),
  fitted_response = round(predict(fit, data.frame(dose_mg = doses)), 1)
)

ctdnaTrend.code:
# Mean ctDNA per arm at each visit week: one row per week, one column per arm.
trend = visits.groupby(["week", "arm"])["ctdna"].mean().unstack("arm")
trend = trend[["Placebo", "Low", "Mid", "High"]].round(2)
trend.index = ["Week %d" % w for w in trend.index]
result = trend

correlations.code:
# Pairwise Pearson correlation of the patient measurements.
cols = ["dose_mg", "response_pct", "ctdna_baseline", "age"]
result = patients[cols].corr().round(2)

about.text:
How this dashboard is built

Three charts are computed on the server from the two inline datasets (96 patients; 480 lab visits):
• Dose–response: an R nls() Emax fit over every patient.
• ctDNA over time: a Python pandas groupby of the visits.
• Correlations: a Python pandas corr() of the patient table.

Click </> Code on any of them to see the exact R or Python code and the CanvasXpress config that draws it. The scatter plot reads the patient table directly, so it has no code step.
